questions.question: What was Catherine the Great's birth name?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states she was born Sophie Auguste Friederike von Anhalt-Zerbst.
Incorrect. Joanna Elisabeth of Holstein-Gottorp was Catherine's mother.
Incorrect. Catherine I of Russia was an earlier empress whose name Catherine took at baptism.
Incorrect. Elizabeth of Russia was the reigning empress who arranged Catherine's marriage to Peter.

questions.question: How long did Catherine the Great reign as Empress of Russia?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states her reign of over 34 years lasted from 9 July 1762 until her death in 1796.
Incorrect. Seven months was the length of Peter III's reign before his deposition.
Incorrect. The article does not state a 10-year reign.
Incorrect. The article does not state a 20-year reign.

questions.question: Where was Catherine born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Catherine was born in the city of Stettin, now known as Szczecin.
Incorrect. Saint Petersburg was where her wedding took place, not her birthplace.
Incorrect. The article does not state she was born in Moscow.
Incorrect. Oranienbaum was the residence of the young court after her marriage.

questions.question: At what age did Catherine marry Peter?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Catherine had recently turned 16 when the marriage took place on 21 August 1745.
Incorrect. She arrived in Russia at age 15, but married the following year at 16.
Incorrect. She met Peter at age 10, but did not marry him then.
Incorrect. The article does not state she married at age 18.

questions.question: Which religion did Catherine convert to upon arriving in Russia?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the Russian Orthodox Church received Sophie as a member and she took the baptismal name Catherine.
Incorrect. Catherine was born a Lutheran but converted to Eastern Orthodoxy despite her father's objections.
Incorrect. The article does not mention conversion to Catholicism.
Incorrect. The article does not mention conversion to Islam.

questions.question: Which institution did Catherine establish as the first state-financed higher education institution for women in Europe?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Catherine established the Smolny Institute of Noble Maidens, the first state-financed higher education institution for women in Europe.
Incorrect. The article does not attribute the founding of the University of Moscow to Catherine.
Incorrect. The article does not mention the St. Petersburg Academy in this context.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a Catherine Palace School.

questions.question: Which territory did Russians colonise under Catherine, becoming the first Europeans to do so?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Russians became the first Europeans to colonise Alaska, establishing Russian America.
Incorrect. Catherine installed a former lover on the throne of Poland, but did not colonise it as the first Europeans.
Incorrect. The Crimean Khanate was annexed, but the article does not describe Russians as the first Europeans to colonise it.
Incorrect. New Russia was colonised with British support along the Black and Azov seas, but Alaska is described as the first European colonisation.

questions.question: What did the Manifesto on Freedom of the Nobility free Russian nobles from?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the manifesto freed Russian nobles from compulsory military or state service.
Incorrect. The article does not mention freedom from payment of taxes.
Incorrect. The article states serfdom continued and was not abolished by this manifesto.
Incorrect. The article does not mention freedom from foreign alliances.

questions.question: Which language was used as the main language of the Russian imperial court until 1812?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the use of French as the main language of the Russian imperial court continued until 1812.
Incorrect. Although Catherine learned Russian, she spoke French in court most circumstances.
Incorrect. German was Catherine's native language, but not the main court language.
Incorrect. The article does not identify Latin as the main court language.
